text:
jia: quick share — ran a small A100 vs H100 sweep for Llama-2-7b (fp16 / q4_k_mixed) across us-west1 / us-east1 / eu-west1. numbers are prefill+decode latency, tokens/sec and a rough $/1M token cost. highlights first: H100 consistently wins latency and tokens/sec, but region egress + spot price variance flips $/1M for some slices. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: nice, did you run the same kernel config? any kernel fallbacks?

matt: ran with the standard infer-runtime flags we use for bringup: `--kernels flash_attn_v2 --kv-cache sharded --batching auto --seq-len 2048`. job invocations:
```
rbench run --model llama-2-7b --gpu h100 --quant q4_k_mixed --region us-west1 --seq 2048 --concurrency 8
rbench run --model llama-2-7b --gpu a100 --quant q4_k_mixed --region us-west1 --seq 2048 --concurrency 8
```

ops-bot: benchmark job 1876543210-01 completed (H100/us-west1), 1876543210-02 completed (A100/us-west1) :white_check_mark:

jia: raw median numbers (us-west1):
- H100 (fp16 -> q4): prefill p50 160ms, decode p50 22ms, tokens/sec 1650, $/1M tokens ~ $0.72
- A100 (fp16 -> q4): prefill p50 220ms, decode p50 30ms, tokens/sec 980, $/1M tokens ~ $1.05
(repeat across 1000 traces, 8-concurrency, seq=2048 single-stream emulation)

ana: those $/1M look optimistic. how are you computing cost? instance-hour assumptions?

jia: simple calc: (instance_hour_cost / (tokens_per_sec * 3600)) * 1e6. used spot-ish pricing we observed during the run: H100-equivalent node $1.8/hr (multi-tenant/dedicated mix), A100 node $1.6/hr. plus ~10% network/infra overhead assumption. numbers changed in eu-west1 because spot premiums were higher there.

sam: interesting — so even though H100 node $/hr slightly higher, tokens/sec delta makes it cheaper. any quality regressions from q4_k_mixed vs fp16?

matt: ran a small eval harness on our LLM-eval slice (summarization + code tasks):
- fp16 baseline: macro acc 72.1
- q4_k_mixed: macro acc 70.5 (-1.6)
- q5_0 (experimental): 71.8 (-0.3)
So q4 shows some small regressions on reasoning/code, but q5_0 looks promising at higher memory but similar perf to q4 in decode latency.

ana: did you try different kernel combinations? flash_attn vs cuBLASLt???

matt: yea — kernel sweep quick notes (us-west1/H100):
- flash_attn_v2 + fused-kv: best latency p50 and p95 for decode.
- cuBLASLt path gave slightly higher prefill but more stable p95 under burst.
- fallback to generic attention spikes single-digit ms but only under odd seq shapes.
Command to repro kernel switch:
```
INFER_KERNEL=cuBLASLt rbench run --model llama-2-7b --gpu h100 --quant q4_k_mixed ...
```

jia: region breakdown (short):
- us-west1: best p50/p95 for H100; low egress; cheapest $/1M in this sweep.
- us-east1: similar latency but spot price variance made A100 occasionally cheaper for sustained throughput.
- eu-west1: H100 still faster, but higher node-hour cost + egress flipped $/1M in favor of A100 for the q4 baseline slices.

sam: any weirdness with KV cache memory pressure on A100 at seq=2048?

matt: yes — A100 with q4_k_mixed and concurrency 12 hit OOM for some traces, required reducing batch size / increasing shard count. H100 handled concurrency 16 without mem OOM.

jia: operational takeaway: for 7b-ish models and seq ~2k, H100 -> better latency/tokens and usually lower $/1M unless region pricing spikes. A100 still attractive for very capacity-constrained markets or where H100 spot is scarce. For production, consider offering both and letting smart-routing pick by cost+latency policy.

ana: follow-ups? can we add a small eval run with q5_0 across regions + kernel sweep, and a perf-run with concurrency ramp to map p95 cliff?

jia: yes — I'll spin that up tomorrow. will attach run ids. thanks for quick look :thumbsup:
